observations: The nine natural family sheets show the same fresh mint torso, white skull/belly and pale-yellow halo. Half-age regions develop between that common first form and the mature endpoint instead of immediately adopting the final palette. The original planar eyes remain in place, with ordinary blinking and occasional idle head tilt visible in some fixtures.

The upper cap faces carry two distinct color regions; small wing lobes carry their corresponding proximal and distal pigments. No unexpected transparent frame, missing material, color bleed or stretched texture was observed in the selected views.

Red two-tone, red shiny, green mono, ruby and natural shiny fixtures retain their inherited skin and regional contrasts with the same relevant shape. The halo stays the developmental species pigment rather than inheriting red/green/ruby genes. Red and natural shiny fixtures visibly show bright reflection highlights in the opened stills, including on the new cap regions; moving-highlight continuity was not reviewed here.

The original central belly, heels and tail remain white on the natural family, or inherited coat-colored on variants. Directional Minecraft light shades white surfaces gray and colors side faces darker; this is visible lighting, not a postprocessed comparison or replacement of the source pigment. Fine glasses rim stippling is visible in the full front/side stills and was also visible in the separately reopened .63 comparator; the glasses assets are unchanged. No new material issue was identified there.

The selected real-evolution frames show the original blue Hero baby orb and blue/yellow baby regions, the actual cocoon, then a fresh white/mint Hero Swim adult with a yellow halo. The late adult back still retains youthful cap proportions and palette despite strong Swim training, rather than appearing immediately mature and violet.
